title: Maximum Profit of Operating a Centennial Wheel
summary: You operate a Centennial Wheel with four gondolas, each capable of holding up to four people.
statement: You operate a Centennial Wheel with four gondolas, each capable of holding up to four people. Rotating the wheel costs runningCost dollars. Customers arrive in batches just before each rotation, and you must rotate to accommodate them. Each customer pays boardingCost dollars to board the gondola closest to the ground and will exit once that gondola reaches the ground again. You can stop the wheel at any time, after which all subsequent rotations are free to ensure all customers are safely served. If there are more than four customers waiting, only four will board the gondola, and the rest will wait for the next rotation. Return the minimum number of rotations needed to maximize your profit, or -1 if no scenario results in a positive profit.
constraints: 1–100,000 arrival batches with 0–10 customers each; costs are positive.
At most four customers board per rotation. Return the earliest rotation with maximum positive profit, or -1.
reference_solution:
def best_wheel_rotation(customers, boarding_cost, running_cost):
 waiting=profit=best=0;answer=-1;rotation=0
 while rotation<len(customers) or waiting:
  if rotation<len(customers):waiting+=customers[rotation]
  boarded=min(4,waiting);waiting-=boarded;rotation+=1;profit+=boarded*boarding_cost-running_cost
  if profit>best:best=profit;answer=rotation
 return answer

Track waiting customers, board four, and update cumulative profit.
Continue after arrivals while anyone waits; update the answer only on a strict new positive maximum.
Simulation preserves arrival order and strict comparison keeps the earliest maximum rotation.
